📌 Fake Customer Support: Help That Comes to Steal

Main Points
⏺ You post a question about a stuck transaction or a locked account
⏺ Within minutes, "support agents" reply or DM you with an offer to help
⏺ This post explains how the scam works and how to reach real support




1️⃣ Core Idea — Scammers watch public chats, comments and social media for people asking for help, then pretend to be the exchange's or wallet's support team.
2️⃣ Why It Happens — When funds look stuck, people are stressed and want a quick fix. A fast, friendly reply from an account with a logo and the right name feels like real help.
3️⃣ Example — You write that your withdrawal is pending. A "support" account DMs you a link to a "verification form" or asks you to "sync your wallet" — and the form asks for your seed phrase.
4️⃣ Red Flags — Support writing to you first, requests for your seed phrase or private key, links to forms outside the official site, remote-access apps, and pressure to act "before the account is frozen".
5️⃣ Practical Rule — Open support only from the official website or app, never from a DM or a reply. Real support will never ask for your seed phrase, and no admin will message you first.
Final Thoughts

The faster someone offers to help, the more carefully you should check who they are. Real support waits for you to come to it.

📌 Cardano introduces on-chain surveys that anyone can independently verify 

🌐 The Cardano Foundation has introduced a new way for developers and community members to conduct surveys directly on the Cardano blockchain, with two surveys already deployed on the network’s mainnet under the CIP-179 standard. Community members Ryan Wiley and Thomas Lindseth developed CIP-179 to address limitations in Cardano’s existing governance tools, which offer relatively few options for gathering detailed feedback from the community.

⚠️ The foundation subsequently contributed to the standard and developed Tessera, an open-source application through which users can create surveys, submit answers and verify published results. Through Cardano’s existing governance Info Actions, community sentiment can be gathered using yes-or-no questions. Stake pool operators (SPOs) have had access to multiple-choice polling through CIP-94 since 2023, although participation is limited to that particular group.

⭐️ CIP-179 supports six standard question formats, including single-choice and multiple-choice questions, rankings, numerical responses, ratings and the allocation of points across several options. Survey organizers could use the system to ask delegated representatives (DReps) how treasury funds should be distributed across development projects or what values they would support for particular network parameters. Each survey is published as a Cardano transaction containing information about its questions, participation requirements and closing date. Respondents then submit individually signed transactions referencing the original survey.

U.S. Army Declares Dark Eagle Hypersonic Missile System Operational After Years of Delays 🚀


The U.S. Army has reached a major milestone in its hypersonic weapons program, officially completing the fielding of its first Long-Range Hypersonic Weapon (LRHW) battery, known as Dark Eagle. 

The announcement came from Lt. Gen. Frank Lozano, the Army’s Program Acquisition Executive for Fires, who says the system is now fully operational and ready for deployment.

“It is fully fielded. It is ready to go,” Lozano told Breaking Defense in a November 19 interview. He described Dark Eagle as a globally deployable capability, adding that the troops assigned to the system now have the equipment and resources needed to operate it.

However, the Army has not disclosed where the first battery is stationed or precisely when it achieved full operational status.

The milestone follows years of setbacks. The Army originally planned to field Dark Eagle in 2023, but technical problems, including difficulties with the launch system, pushed the deadline back. 

A revised September 2025 target was also missed. As recently as October 2026, reports indicated that the battery was still undergoing fielding activities and required additional training and readiness work.

Dark Eagle is designed to travel at hypersonic speeds, exceeding Mach 5, and provide the Army with a long-range conventional strike capability. Its development has been closely coordinated with the Navy’s Conventional Prompt Strike program, which uses the same hypersonic glide body technology.

Meanwhile, the Army is moving ahead with its second and third batteries. Lozano declined to provide deployment timelines, citing operational security, but confirmed that production of the third battery is already more than halfway complete. He expects the next two units to reach full operational capability faster than the first.

The program still faces manufacturing and quality-control challenges. A July Government Accountability Office report highlighted production difficulties at Lockheed Martin, prompting concerns about manufacturing standards and the consistency of testing.

Looking ahead, the Army is also considering bringing additional contractors into the program. Lozano said having multiple suppliers could improve production flexibility and reduce dependence on a single manufacturer.

The first Dark Eagle battery marks an important step in the Pentagon’s effort to expand America’s hypersonic weapons capabilities, although questions surrounding production, delivery schedules and long-term readiness remain.

📣 European Banking Authority (EBA) warns of stablecoin risks and calls for tighter DeFi oversight 

⚠️ The European Banking Authority (EBA) has identified stablecoins as central to decentralized finance (DeFi) while renewing its call for the European Commission to examine whether cryptocurrency service providers facilitating access to lending protocols should face additional regulatory requirements. The regulator found that European consumer participation in DeFi remains limited, although access is becoming easier through cryptocurrency platforms and applications powered by artificial intelligence. Meanwhile, 42% of European-based investors expect to engage with DeFi by 2028, according to figures cited by the EBA.

🔗 The EBA found that stablecoins, including certain EMTs issued under the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), are extensively used to facilitate borrowing, lending and trading activities.Users can deposit stablecoins into lending protocols to make funds available to borrowers, use them as collateral against loans or exchange them for other digital assets through decentralized trading platforms.

⚡️ Under MiCA, electronic money tokens are cryptocurrencies designed to maintain a stable value by referencing a single official currency, such as the euro or the U.S. dollar. The use of self-hosted cryptocurrency wallets, through which individuals typically interact directly with DeFi protocols, remains relatively low across EU member states compared with other major financial markets. Germany and France recorded the highest levels of DeFi interaction within the European Union but ranked 18th and 19th globally, respectively. Spain placed 26th, while India led the international rankings, followed by the United States. The United Kingdom ranked 12th.
